title: The Damaged Life: Frankfurt, Vienna, and the Long Way Back to the Institute

segments.name: The House on the Schöne Aussicht

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, born on the Schöne Aussicht
stops.date_confidence: attested. Birth date and the address Schöne Aussicht 9 both given by the German Wikipedia article on Adorno; the coordinates here are the Nominatim geocode of that address, correcting a figure in the research pool that landed roughly 1.4 km downriver.
stops.campa: On the Main embankment at Schöne Aussicht 9, in a house where the wine trade pays for the piano, a son is born to Oscar Wiesengrund and named Theodor Ludwig. The father exports wine under the firm Wiesengrund & Co. The mother, Maria Calvelli-Adorno, has sung professionally, and her sister Agathe lives with them and plays. The boy grows up between two women who make music and one man who makes money out of Rhine vintages. In 1914 the family crosses the river to Seeheimer Strasse 19 in Oberrad, and the four-hands piano goes with them.
suggested_refs: Schöne Aussicht 9, Frankfurt am Main, the birth house on the Main embankment
Seeheimer Strasse 19, Oberrad, the family's second Frankfurt house from 1914
sources: German Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno' (address, parents, 1914 move)
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

stops.name: Sachsenhausen, the Gymnasium and the Saturday Kant
stops.date_confidence: school years 1913-1921 attested; the Kracauer readings are [R], reported in the biographical tradition and not confirmed in the encyclopedia entries consulted. The school's name is anachronistic before 1917: the Sachsenhausen Gymnasium bore the name Kaiser-Wilhelms-Gymnasium only from that year, and became the Freiherr-vom-Stein-Schule in 1945. Coordinates are the Sachsenhausen building, correcting a pool figure that sat on the wrong bank of the Main. Month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He passes through the Sachsenhausen Gymnasium, renamed for Kaiser Wilhelm during his time in it, and takes the Abitur in 1921 at seventeen, two years early. From about fifteen he spends Saturday afternoons with Siegfried Kracauer, an editor at the Frankfurter Zeitung fourteen years his senior, reading Immanuel Kant's Critique of Pure Reason a line at a time. Kracauer teaches him to read the first Critique as a text with a social wound in it, and to read a popular song or a newspaper horoscope by the same method. No source records which room they sat in.
stops.quote: Talent is above all perhaps nothing other than serendipitously sublimated rage.
stops.quote_source: Minima Moralia, trans. Dennis Redmond, online edition at marxists.org (aphorisms 51-100); written four decades after these Saturdays
suggested_refs: The Freiherr-vom-Stein-Schule, Schweizer Strasse 87, Frankfurt-Sachsenhausen, formerly the Kaiser-Wilhelms-Gymnasium
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno' (Kaiser-Wilhelm Gymnasium, 1913-1921)
German Wikipedia, 'Freiherr-vom-Stein-Schule (Frankfurt am Main)' (renaming dates)
Biographical tradition on the Kracauer readings, unconfirmed in SEP or Wikipedia [R]

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, matriculation under Cornelius
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day are a default for ordering. Coordinates are the Bockenheim campus main building at Mertonstrasse 17, correcting a pool figure repeated across eight geography entries that sat some 350 m southeast of it.
stops.campa: He enters the University of Frankfurt, founded four years earlier, and registers for philosophy, sociology, psychology, and music at once. Hans Cornelius, a neo-Kantian who also paints and composes, takes him into his seminar. Two older students are already working there: Friedrich Pollock, and Max Horkheimer, a manufacturer's son from Stuttgart who had been taken out of the Gymnasium and put to work on the floor of his father's factory. Adorno is eighteen. The collaboration with Horkheimer that begins in that seminar room runs forty-eight years, to the end of his life.
suggested_refs: The Jügelhaus, Mertonstrasse 17, the Bockenheim campus of the Johann Wolfgang Goethe University
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno'
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Theodor W. Adorno' (Cornelius as principal teacher)

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, Kracauer brings Benjamin
stops.date_confidence: [R] on the date and setting. German Wikipedia says he met Benjamin 'durch Vermittlung Kracauers als Student', which places it in Frankfurt during the student years; English Wikipedia's Benjamin article attaches the acquaintance to 1923. The research pool's own entry said 'Germany' generically. Year left soft at 1922-1923; month and day defaulted.
stops.campa: Kracauer brings him to Walter Benjamin, eleven years older, a scholar with no post and no prospect of getting one. The two begin a correspondence that will run to Benjamin's death and will hold some of the hardest letters either man ever writes: about Baudelaire, about the Paris arcades, about how much theory a piece of dialectical description must carry before it has earned its images. What the record does not fix is the day. German and English sources between them put the meeting somewhere in 1922 or 1923, in Frankfurt, through Kracauer.
suggested_refs: The Adorno-Benjamin correspondence, published as Briefwechsel 1928-1940
sources: German Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno'
English Wikipedia, 'Walter Benjamin' (1923 acquaintance)

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, the doctorate on Husserl
stops.date_confidence: year and supervisor attested by the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy; month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: At twenty-one he defends a dissertation titled Die Transzendenz des Dinglichen und Noematischen in Husserls Phänomenologie, written under Cornelius. It is a young man's book and he never publishes it in that form. Phenomenology will hold him for a quarter of a century, and the Metakritik that finally settles his account with Husserl is drafted in England and printed in 1956. He is twenty-one and a doctor of philosophy of the University of Frankfurt, and what he wants to do is compose.
suggested_refs: Zur Metakritik der Erkenntnistheorie (1956), the eventual settling of the Husserl account
sources: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Theodor W. Adorno'
English Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

segments.name: The Composer He Did Not Become

stops.name: Vienna, the room in the Pension Luisenheim
stops.date_confidence: sources conflict on the month and the conflict is left standing: German Wikipedia says 'Im März 1925 zog Adorno nach Wien' and names the Pension Luisenheim in the ninth district; English Wikipedia says February 1925. The March date is used here because it comes from the source that names the lodging. Coordinates are the canonical Alsergrund pin the atlas already carries for the ninth district, not the pension building, which is not independently located.
stops.campa: He has heard excerpts of Wozzeck in Frankfurt and introduced himself to its composer on the spot. Now he moves to Vienna and takes a room in the Pension Luisenheim in the ninth district. He comes intending to become a professional composer and expects to stay. The city he walks into is Schoenberg's city, Karl Kraus reads aloud in its halls, and the twelve-tone method is four years old. German and English accounts disagree over whether he arrived in February of 1925 or in March.
suggested_refs: The Pension Luisenheim, Vienna IX (Alsergrund), his lodging from 1925
sources: German Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno' (March 1925, Pension Luisenheim)
English Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno' (February 1925)

stops.name: Hietzing, lessons with Alban Berg
stops.date_confidence: the fact of composition study with Berg in Vienna in 1925 is attested (SEP, IEP). The specific Trauttmansdorffgasse address in Hietzing is [R], established musicological record for Berg rather than a source consulted here. Month and day are a default for ordering.
stops.campa: Alban Berg takes him as a composition pupil, and he will call Berg his master and teacher for the rest of his life. Piano with Eduard Steuermann, friendship with the violinist Rudolf Kolisch, and the whole Schoenberg orbit come with the arrangement. He writes songs and pieces and they are performed. They do not make him a composer of the first rank, and he is intelligent enough to know it before anyone tells him. Berg's Hietzing address is a matter of musicological record rather than of anything Adorno himself set down.
suggested_refs: Alban Berg's apartment in the Trauttmansdorffgasse, Vienna XIII (Hietzing)
sources: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Theodor W. Adorno'
Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Adorno'

stops.name: Berlin, the Karplus flat
stops.date_confidence: [R] throughout. The marriage is documented; the meeting with Gretel Karplus is dated to Berlin in 1923 only by tradition, unconfirmed in the encyclopedia entries consulted, and the pool could not verify the Bloch-circle framing against any atlas file. The 1928 date here orders the Berlin years and is not a claim about a first meeting. Coordinates are the canonical Berlin pin.
stops.campa: In Berlin he keeps a second life among Benjamin's and Ernst Bloch's people, and there he is close to Margarete Karplus, called Gretel. She will become his wife, his shorthand writer, his editor, and after 1969 the assembler of his last book out of the typescripts he leaves unfinished. Tradition dates their first meeting to 1923. No source consulted here confirms it, and nothing read for this file records what passed between the two of them in the fourteen years before the wedding.
suggested_refs: The Adorno-Gretel Karplus correspondence, Briefwechsel 1930-1940
sources: Tradition, unconfirmed in SEP or Wikipedia [R]
English Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno' (marriage attested)

stops.name: Vienna, the Musikblätter des Anbruch
stops.date_confidence: [R]. The editorial involvement is placed at 1928-1930 by the research pool on the strength of SEP plus the standard bibliography of his Vienna music criticism; no primary masthead was consulted. Month and day defaulted to 01. This stop is ordered after the Berlin stop of 1928 so that dates within the segment do not run backward.
stops.campa: He joins the editorial circle of the Musikblätter des Anbruch and writes concert and opera criticism, defending Schoenberg and Berg and attacking Igor Stravinsky, Hindemith, and commercial jazz with the same instrument. The criticism is where the composer's training goes once the composing does not take. He is learning to hear a chord as a social fact: who is licensed to write it, what a market will pay for it, which listener it flatters. The verdicts he hands down in these pages he will still be defending in 1949.
suggested_refs: Musikblätter des Anbruch, Vienna, his principal outlet for music criticism in the late 1920s
Philosophie der neuen Musik (1949), where the Schoenberg-Stravinsky verdict is restated at book length
sources: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Theodor W. Adorno'
Standard bibliographic record of the Vienna-period music criticism [R]

segments.name: The Venia Legendi and the Closing Door

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, the habilitation withdrawn
stops.date_confidence: attested by SEP as to the withdrawal and the manuscript's subject; month and day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He submits a habilitation manuscript, Der Begriff des Unbewussten in der transzendentalen Seelenlehre, on the concept of the unconscious in transcendental psychology. Cornelius and Paul Tillich signal that it will not pass, and he withdraws it rather than be refused. The failure costs him four years and shuts a university door he had assumed would open of its own accord. He keeps writing music criticism in Vienna and Frankfurt and does not treat the rejection anywhere in print as a wound. What he does with the four years is read Kierkegaard.
suggested_refs: Der Begriff des Unbewussten in der transzendentalen Seelenlehre, the withdrawn first habilitation
sources: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, Kierkegaard and the venia legendi
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month: English Wikipedia gives 'received habilitation in February 1931'; SEP names Tillich as sponsor. Day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: With Paul Tillich sponsoring him this time, he submits Kierkegaard: Konstruktion des Ästhetischen and receives the venia legendi in February 1931. The book reads Kierkegaard's interiority as a bourgeois apartment, the furniture of a nineteenth-century rentier mistaken by its occupant for the architecture of the soul. It appears as a book in 1933, the same year the licence it earned him is taken away, and it sells almost nothing. He is twenty-seven and a Privatdozent.
suggested_refs: Kierkegaard: Konstruktion des Ästhetischen (1933), the habilitation as published
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno'
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, the actuality of philosophy
stops.date_confidence: [R] as to the exact day. SEP catalogues 'Die Aktualität der Philosophie' as the inaugural address of 7 May 1931; no primary programme or faculty record was consulted here.
stops.campa: On the seventh of May he gives his inaugural lecture as Privatdozent, Die Aktualität der Philosophie. He tells the faculty that philosophy can no longer take reality whole, that no thought is going to close over the world and hold it there, and that what is left is interpretation: small constructed constellations, arranged and rearranged until an image gives up its meaning. It is a programme he will keep for thirty-five years without once calling it a system. The teaching it licenses lasts two years.
suggested_refs: Die Aktualität der Philosophie, inaugural lecture, Frankfurt, 7 May 1931
sources: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, the Viktoria-Allee and the Zeitschrift
stops.date_confidence: attested by SEP as to the 1932 essay and the Zeitschrift venue; month and day defaulted. Coordinates corrected to Senckenberganlage 26, the Nominatim geocode of the pre-1933 Institute address, which German Wikipedia spells Viktoria-Allee, not Victoria-Allee as the research pool had it.
stops.campa: He is not yet on the Institute's payroll, but the Zeitschrift für Sozialforschung, edited out of the building on the Viktoria-Allee, becomes his main venue. Zur gesellschaftlichen Lage der Musik appears there in 1932 and shifts his criticism off aesthetics and onto a sociology of listening: what a hit song does to the ear that consumes it, and who takes the money. Max Horkheimer has been director for two years and is building a journal capable of outliving its own country.
suggested_refs: Zeitschrift für Sozialforschung, the Institute journal edited from Viktoria-Allee (today Senckenberganlage)
sources: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Theodor W. Adorno'
German Wikipedia, 'Institut für Sozialforschung' (pre-1933 address)

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, the licence revoked
stops.date_confidence: the revocation in 1933 under the racial legislation is attested by SEP; September is the pool's month and is not separately confirmed, so treat it as [R]. Coordinates are the canonical Frankfurt Institute pin the atlas already carries, the same pin Max Horkheimer's file uses for the building's seizure in March 1933.
stops.campa: On the thirtieth of January the government changes. In September his venia legendi is revoked under the racial legislation and the teaching stops. Police search the Institute's building and his family's house, and the Reich Chamber of Literature will later reject his application on the ground that he is not an Aryan. The Institute's money has already gone to a Geneva foundation and Horkheimer with it. Adorno stays in Germany another year, travelling, arguing with himself over whether the thing might yet pass.
suggested_refs: The Law for the Restoration of the Professional Civil Service, 7 April 1933, under which the Frankfurt purges ran
sources: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Theodor W. Adorno'
English Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

stops.name: Oxford, registered as an advanced student
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month: English Wikipedia gives 'Registered at Merton College, Oxford in June 1934', with the Oxford period running to February 1938. The season of his departure from Germany is contradictory in the sources and is not resolved here: SEP says spring 1934, English Wikipedia says autumn 1934 while dating the Merton registration to June. Day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: The Academic Assistance Council places him at Merton College as an advanced student, a status which means that a doctor of philosophy of thirty is enrolled as a pupil. He works under Gilbert Ryle on a critique of Husserl that will not see print for twenty-two years. Oxford gives him no permanent post; he writes of cultural isolation and crosses back to the Continent whenever he can arrange it. English and German accounts disagree over whether he left Germany in the spring of 1934 or the autumn. Both put him here in June.
suggested_refs: Merton College, Oxford, where he was enrolled June 1934 to February 1938
The Academic Assistance Council, which placed refugee scholars in British universities from 1933
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

stops.name: Paris, the visits to Benjamin
stops.date_confidence: [R] entirely. The research dossier records repeated trips to Paris across the Oxford years to see Benjamin and Horkheimer; no source consulted here fixes a date to any single visit, and the 1936 date is an ordering device. Max Horkheimer's own Paris stop of October 1937, his last meeting with Benjamin, is a separate event on Horkheimer's file and is not claimed here for Adorno. Coordinates are the canonical Paris pin.
stops.campa: He crosses to Paris to see Benjamin, who is living on Institute stipends in rooms he cannot afford and assembling the arcades material. The two argue in person and then go on arguing by letter, where each has more room. Adorno's position is that Benjamin's images need theory underneath them or they will be read as mysticism; Benjamin's is that theory laid over an image kills the image. Neither concedes anything. How many such crossings there were, and when, the record consulted here does not say.
suggested_refs: Benjamin's Passagenwerk, in progress in Paris through the years of Adorno's Oxford exile
sources: Research dossier only, unconfirmed against any consulted source [R]
Max Horkheimer journey file, stop of 1937-10-01, Paris (a distinct event)

stops.name: Oxford, Über Jazz signed Hektor Rottweiler
stops.date_confidence: the essay, the year, the journal, and the pseudonym are all attested verbatim by German Wikipedia: 'den Aufsatz Über Jazz, der 1936 in der Zeitschrift für Sozialforschung unter dem Pseudonym Hektor Rottweiler erschien'. The rationale for the pseudonym is [R] and is not given by that source. Month and day are an ordering default.
stops.campa: He publishes Über Jazz in the Zeitschrift für Sozialforschung under the name Hektor Rottweiler. The essay treats syncopation as a licensed deviation sold back to the listener as freedom, and improvisation as a thing standardized in advance of being played. It has been read ever since as the ugliest piece he wrote, and he never retracts it. Why he used a pseudonym is a separate question: the account that it shielded a man still crossing into Germany is plausible, and it is not in the source that attests the name.
stops.quote: The culture industry perpetually cheats its consumers of what it perpetually promises.
stops.quote_source: Horkheimer and Adorno, 'The Culture Industry: Enlightenment as Mass Deception,' in Dialectic of Enlightenment, online text at marxists.org; a co-authored formulation of 1944, eight years after the jazz essay
suggested_refs: Über Jazz, Zeitschrift für Sozialforschung V (1936), published as by Hektor Rottweiler
sources: German Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno' (title, year, journal, pseudonym)
English Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno' ('On Jazz', 1936)

stops.name: Paddington, the register office
stops.date_confidence: attested. English Wikipedia gives the date 8 September 1937; German Wikipedia specifies the venue as 'im Standesamt des Districts Paddington'. Coordinates are the Paddington register district, correcting a research-pool figure that marked Charing Cross, some 4 km away.
stops.campa: Fourteen years after Berlin, Theodor and Gretel are married at the register office of the district of Paddington on the eighth of September. He is thirty-three: a Privatdozent of a university that has expelled him and an advanced student of one that will not hire him. Gretel has come out of Berlin by way of London and has been waiting on the paperwork as long as he has. The marriage runs to the end of his life, and what the English record gives of the ceremony is a district and a date. Five months later they take ship for New York together.
stops.quote: Love you will find only where you may show yourself weak without provoking strength.
stops.quote_source: Minima Moralia, aphorism 122 ('Monograms'), trans. E. F. N. Jephcott; the same German rendered by Dennis Redmond at marxists.org as 'You are loved, solely where you may show yourself as weak, without provoking strength'
suggested_refs: Paddington register office, London, the marriage of 8 September 1937
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno' (date)
German Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno' (Standesamt Paddington)

stops.name: New York, the Institute at Columbia
stops.date_confidence: attested. English Wikipedia gives the sailing date of 16 February 1938 and the New York period as running to November 1941. Coordinates are the canonical Morningside Heights pin the atlas already carries for the Institute in exile, shared with the Horkheimer and Marcuse files.
stops.campa: He sails for New York on the sixteenth of February, brought over by Max Horkheimer, who has finally secured him a place in the Institute's American research network. The Institute sits beside Columbia in Morningside Heights, and the men around it are Horkheimer, Leo Löwenthal, Friedrich Pollock, and Herbert Marcuse. After fifteen years of standing adjacent to the Institute, Adorno is inside it. His English at this point is not good enough to lecture in.
suggested_refs: The Institute for Social Research in exile at Columbia University, Morningside Heights
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

stops.name: Newark, the Princeton Radio Research Project
stops.date_confidence: the appointment, the funder, and the Newark administration are attested by SEP and English Wikipedia ('Princeton Radio Project in Newark, New Jersey'); the exact office address is not established and the month is an ordering default.
stops.campa: Paul Lazarsfeld hires him to run the music division of the Rockefeller-funded Princeton Radio Research Project, administered out of an office in Newark. He is asked to measure what listeners like. He studies instead the plugging of songs, the standardization of the product, and the pseudo-individualization that makes each standard tune feel to its hearer like a private possession. His reports overrun the formats they were commissioned for, and his English is still difficult enough to slow him down. The music unit loses its funding in 1941.
stops.quote: Amusement under late capitalism is the prolongation of work.
stops.quote_source: Horkheimer and Adorno, 'The Culture Industry: Enlightenment as Mass Deception,' in Dialectic of Enlightenment, online text at marxists.org; written after the radio project had ended
suggested_refs: The Princeton Radio Research Project, Newark, and Adorno's memorandum 'On Popular Music' (1941)
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

stops.name: New York, the letter about Baudelaire
stops.date_confidence: [R]. The Institute's rejection of Benjamin's Baudelaire essay in 1938 comes from the research dossier and could not be confirmed against any atlas file or consulted encyclopedia entry; no Benjamin journey file yet exists to check it against. Month and day are ordering defaults.
stops.campa: The Institute sends back Benjamin's Baudelaire essay rather than print it in the Zeitschrift, and the letter that carries the verdict is Adorno's. He tells his friend that the material stands at the crossroads of magic and positivism, that the images arrive unmediated, that facts set beside facts have not yet begun to think. Benjamin revises. The exchange becomes one of the long quarrels of twentieth-century criticism and its terms are argued over still. It is the dossier that dates it to 1938.
suggested_refs: Adorno's letter to Benjamin of 10 November 1938 on 'The Paris of the Second Empire in Baudelaire'

stops.name: Pacific Palisades, the move west
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month by English Wikipedia ('Moved to Pacific Palisades, Los Angeles in November 1941'), with the Los Angeles period running to October 1949. The specific rented house is not identified in any consulted source. Coordinates are the canonical Pacific Palisades pin shared with Max Horkheimer's file.
stops.campa: Adorno and Gretel move to Pacific Palisades in November to live near the Horkheimers. The neighbourhood holds Thomas Mann, Heinrich Mann, Bertolt Brecht, Hanns Eisler, Lion Feuchtwanger, Fritz Lang, and Arnold Schoenberg: a German literary and musical culture reassembled inside a hillside suburb full of lemon trees. After Pearl Harbor he is an enemy alien, under curfew and restricted in how far he may travel from the house. The aphorisms of Minima Moralia are written inside that radius.
suggested_refs: The Pacific Palisades émigré colony, 1940-1949
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

stops.name: Pacific Palisades, the dictation of the Fragments
stops.date_confidence: the composition period 1942-1944 in Los Angeles is attested by SEP and by the publication record of Philosophische Fragmente (1944) and Dialektik der Aufklärung (Querido, 1947). Month and day are ordering defaults. The quoted sentence is verified in that exact wording by SEP and by English Wikipedia's article on the book, both citing the Jephcott translation, Stanford UP 2002, p. xviii, which is the Introduction and not the opening of the 'Concept of Enlightenment' chapter as the research pool's citation had it.
stops.campa: He and Horkheimer compose by talking, in a hillside suburb of the industry the book will end up describing. One speaks, the other objects, Gretel takes it down in shorthand and types the result, and the sentences are worked over until neither man can find the seam. Out of it comes Dialectic of Enlightenment: the thesis that myth was already enlightenment and that enlightenment falls back into myth, and a chapter on the culture industry naming the standardized product and the administered hour of leisure.
stops.quote: Myth is already enlightenment, and enlightenment reverts to mythology.
stops.quote_source: Horkheimer and Adorno, Dialectic of Enlightenment: Philosophical Fragments, trans. Edmund Jephcott (Stanford University Press, 2002), p. xviii
suggested_refs: The culture industry chapter, 'Enlightenment as Mass Deception', jointly signed by Horkheimer and Adorno

stops.name: Hollywood, Fritz Lang and Hanns Eisler
stops.date_confidence: the Eisler collaboration and the single-name first edition are attested by English Wikipedia, though the pool tagged the entry [R]; the friendship with Fritz Lang comes from the research dossier and is not confirmed in the consulted sources, so it is [R]. Coordinates are the canonical Hollywood pin from Fritz Lang's own file. Month and day are ordering defaults.
stops.campa: He goes down into Hollywood, where Fritz Lang has been working since 1936 and Hanns Eisler is scoring pictures. With Eisler he writes Composing for the Films out of Rockefeller-funded research: an analysis of what music is doing when it is laid under an image to manage an audience's nerves. Eisler's politics make the credit dangerous, and the first Oxford University Press edition carries Eisler's name alone. The friendship with Lang is reported in the dossier and is not confirmed in the sources consulted here.
stops.quote: The triumph of advertising in the culture industry is that consumers feel compelled to buy and use its products even though they see through them.
stops.quote_source: Horkheimer and Adorno, 'The Culture Industry: Enlightenment as Mass Deception,' in Dialectic of Enlightenment, online text at marxists.org
suggested_refs: Composing for the Films (Oxford University Press, 1947), first issued under Eisler's name only
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

stops.name: Los Angeles, naturalized
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested by English Wikipedia ('Naturalized as US citizen in November 1943'); the day is unknown and defaulted to 01. The courthouse is not identified in any consulted source, so the coordinates mark the downtown Los Angeles federal district generically and are [R] as to the specific building.
stops.campa: He becomes a citizen of the United States in November, which ends his standing as an enemy alien and gives him back the right to travel. The name on the papers is the one he has been using in America, Adorno, his mother's name, with Wiesengrund reduced to the middle initial he will publish under for the rest of his life. Ten years after the Frankfurt faculty struck him off, he takes another country's citizenship in a downtown federal building. No source consulted here names the building.
suggested_refs: The FBI file kept on Adorno through the Los Angeles years
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

stops.name: New York, the hectograph and then Querido
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the May 1944 hectograph and the 1947 Querido edition. Place corrected: the research pool put the mimeograph in Los Angeles, but English Wikipedia's article on Dialectic of Enlightenment gives the 1944 hectograph 'Philosophische Fragmente' as issued in New York by the Institute for Social Research. Written in Los Angeles, circulated from New York. Day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: The book is written in California and issued out of New York. In May the Institute hectographs Philosophische Fragmente and circulates it privately among people it trusts; the revised trade edition comes out in 1947 from Querido in Amsterdam, a Dutch house publishing German exile literature. Between the mimeograph and the book the war ends, the camps are opened, and the two authors read what the newspapers print about them. The title changes to Dialektik der Aufklärung and Philosophische Fragmente drops to a subtitle.

stops.name: Pacific Palisades, Minima Moralia
stops.date_confidence: the dedication to Horkheimer's fiftieth birthday and the 1951 publication are attested by English Wikipedia; Horkheimer was born 14 February 1895, which fixes the fiftieth to 14 February 1945, and that date is used here to order the segment. The composition span is corrected from the pool's 'chiefly 1944-47': English Wikipedia's article on Minima Moralia says he began in 1944 and completed it in 1949.
stops.campa: He begins the aphorisms in 1944 as a present for Horkheimer's fiftieth birthday and does not finish them until 1949. They are notes from inside the damaged life: on giving presents, on the shape of doors, on what becomes of a man who has lost the language he thinks in, on why the private sphere is no refuge from whatever wrecked the public one. Reflexionen aus dem beschädigten Leben, reflections from damaged life, is the subtitle he puts on the book.
stops.quote: There is no right life in the wrong one.
stops.quote_source: Minima Moralia, aphorism 18 ('Asylum for the Homeless'), trans. Dennis Redmond, online edition at marxists.org; rendered by E. F. N. Jephcott as 'Wrong life cannot be lived rightly'
suggested_refs: Minima Moralia: Reflexionen aus dem beschädigten Leben, written 1944-1949, published 1951

stops.name: Berkeley, the F-scale
stops.date_confidence: the collaboration, the funder, the series, and the 1950 publication are attested by English Wikipedia. The place is [R]: the pool attests only 'United States', and Berkeley is the standard account of where the Public Opinion Study team worked, not something confirmed here. Month and day are ordering defaults; the fieldwork ran through the mid-1940s and the book appeared in 1950.
stops.campa: With Else Frenkel-Brunswik, Daniel Levinson, and R. Nevitt Sanford he works on the study financed by the American Jewish Committee under the series title Studies in Prejudice. They build questionnaires, score interviews, and construct the F-scale, a measure of the disposition to submit upward and strike downward, resting on Sigmund Freud's account of character and of the ego ideal. Nine years after leaving the country that produced that disposition, he is measuring it in the country that took him in.
stops.quote: Anti-Semitism is the rumor about the Jews.
stops.quote_source: Minima Moralia, trans. Dennis Redmond, online edition at marxists.org (aphorisms 51-100)

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, standing in for Horkheimer
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month. English Wikipedia gives 'Left America on October 31, 1949'; the pool and SEP put the Frankfurt return in October 1949. Coordinates are the canonical university pin the atlas already carries, shared with Horkheimer's file. Day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He returns to Frankfurt in October to stand in for Horkheimer at the university, into a city of rubble and denazification questionnaires. The chair is the one the racial legislation took from him sixteen years earlier. He does not settle at once: for four more years he crosses back and forth over the Atlantic, holding an American citizenship he has no intention of surrendering. What he finds in the German lecture rooms is an audience that has heard nothing since 1933 and knows it.

stops.name: Darmstadt, the Kranichstein summer courses
stops.date_confidence: the span is contradictory between sources and the contradiction is not resolved: the research dossier gave 1951-1958, while German Wikipedia says he took part 'zwischen 1950 und 1966 als Referent und Kursleiter nahezu regelmässig'. The German figure is used here as the better-sourced one. Month and day are ordering defaults; the presence of Boulez, Stockhausen, and Nono at Darmstadt is standard record and was not re-verified against a primary programme.
stops.campa: He comes to the Kranichstein summer courses at Darmstadt as lecturer and course leader and keeps coming back, nearly every year, for sixteen years. The young composers there are Pierre Boulez, Karlheinz Stockhausen, and Luigi Nono, and they are building total serialism out of the Vienna he studied in. He tells them a technique carried to full rationalization turns into the opposite of freedom. They tell him he has stopped listening. The argument is never settled and neither side stops attending.

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, the house on the Senckenberganlage
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: German Wikipedia's article on the Institut für Sozialforschung gives the formal reopening as 14 November 1951, and Max Horkheimer's own file carries the same date at the same coordinates. Those canonical coordinates are used here, correcting a research-pool figure some 900 m off the building.
stops.campa: The rebuilt Institute for Social Research opens on the fourteenth of November in a new building on the Senckenberganlage. Adorno is deputy director under Horkheimer and will later be director alongside him. The Institute runs surveys, group experiments, and industrial studies, and does more than any other body to make empirical sociology a German university subject. Frankfurters will end up calling the traffic light on the corner the Adorno-Ampel, after the man who crossed there.

stops.name: Beverly Hills, the Hacker Psychiatric Foundation
stops.date_confidence: attested by SEP: '1952-53 as research director at the Hacker Psychiatric Foundation in Beverly Hills to retain US citizenship'. Month and day are ordering defaults and the Foundation's street address is not established. The August 1953 return date is dossier-cited and consistent with SEP's account of the Frankfurt professorship, but was not separately re-verified.
stops.campa: To keep the American citizenship he crosses back once more and spends the year as research director of the Hacker Psychiatric Foundation in Beverly Hills. The residence requirement is the whole reason for the year, and the record states it that plainly. It puts a German philosopher back on a California payroll, a short drive from the suburb where he wrote the book about the damaged life. In August 1953 he returns to Frankfurt and stays there, keeping the passport he crossed an ocean to protect.

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, the chair and the directorship
stops.date_confidence: the progression from ausserplanmässiger Professor (1950) through a further step (1953) to a full professorship of philosophy and sociology (1956), and the 1958 directorship of the Institute, are attested by English Wikipedia and SEP taken together; the pool notes the exact year of the full chair was not isolated in the fetched text. stops.campa: His appointments climb: ausserplanmässiger Professor in 1950, a further step in 1953, and in 1956 a full professorship of philosophy and sociology. In 1958 he takes over the direction of the Institute outright. He is by now the most visible intellectual in the Federal Republic, constantly on the radio, lecturing to halls that overflow into the corridors, and the students coming out of his seminars in these years include Jürgen Habermas. He is fifty-five.

stops.name: Tübingen, Popper across the table
stops.date_confidence: the 1961 Tübingen conference of the German Sociological Association, the opening papers by Adorno and Popper, and the 1969 collected volume Der Positivismusstreit in der deutschen Soziologie are standard record and corroborated by the dossier; the month and day here are ordering defaults and no primary conference programme was consulted.
stops.campa: At the sociologists' conference in Tübingen he and Karl Popper open the proceedings with papers that do not meet. Popper says Critical Theory totalizes speculatively and offers nothing that could ever be shown false. Adorno says positivism takes for a natural given what a society produced, and that a method blind to that is an ideology carrying statistics. Neither man answers the other's paper. Jürgen Habermas and Hans Albert take the fight up afterward. The papers and the replies are collected in 1969 as Der Positivismusstreit in der deutschen Soziologie.
suggested_refs: Der Positivismusstreit in der deutschen Soziologie (1969), collecting the Tübingen papers and the replies
sources: Standard record of the 1961 Tübingen conference, corroborated by the research dossier

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, Erziehung nach Auschwitz
stops.date_confidence: [R] as to the date. The pool attests the broadcast lecture and the year 1966 but flags the exact broadcast date as unconfirmed against any primary archive, and supplies no month or day; both are defaulted to 01 for ordering only.
stops.campa: He goes into a radio studio and says that the first demand upon all education is that Auschwitz not happen again, that this comes before anything else, and that he holds it beneath discussion to have to justify it. He talks about the coldness that made the murderers possible, about the pressure to conform, about what a schooling would have to do to a child to leave that child incapable of it. It is a broadcast rather than a lecture. It goes out to the country that did it, driving to work.

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, Negative Dialektik
stops.date_confidence: year attested by SEP and English Wikipedia; month and day defaulted to 01 and the stop is placed after the radio lecture for narrative order only, since neither event has a fixed date in the sources consulted. The Minima Moralia sentence quoted here is verified in the Dennis Redmond online translation; Jephcott renders it 'The whole is the false'.
stops.campa: Negative Dialektik appears, the book he has been circling since the inaugural lecture of 1931. Its target is identity thinking: the operation by which a concept swallows the thing it names and then reports that nothing was lost. Against it he sets a dialectic that refuses to resolve, keeping the non-identical outside the concept where it can still raise an objection. Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel had written that the whole is the true; Adorno had already turned that sentence over. Here he states a new categorical imperative, imposed by Hitler upon unfree mankind: to arrange thought and action so that Auschwitz not repeat itself.
stops.quote_source: Minima Moralia, aphorism 29 ('Dwarf Fruit'), trans. Dennis Redmond, online edition at marxists.org
suggested_refs: Negative Dialektik (Suhrkamp, 1966)
sources: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, the police at the Institute
stops.date_confidence: the episode is attested and the breach with Marcuse is corroborated by SEP, but two dates are in the sources and the conflict is left standing: German Wikipedia's Adorno article supports 31 January 1969, while its article on Hans-Jürgen Krahl dates the same occupation to 7 January 1969. Neither source gives the figure of seventy-six arrests that the dossier supplies, so that count is dropped here. Krahl's prosecution is confirmed, with Adorno summoned as a witness on 18 July 1969. Coordinates are the canonical Institute pin, shared with Horkheimer's and Marcuse's files.
stops.campa: Students led by Hans-Jürgen Krahl, who had sat in his seminars, occupy the Institute on the Senckenberganlage to run a strike out of it. Adorno and Ludwig von Friedeburg telephone the police. The occupiers are carried out and arrested and most are released the same evening; Krahl is held and later tried, and Adorno is summoned to that trial in July as a witness. Herbert Marcuse writes to him from California that this is not what critical theory was for. The two men never repair it.
suggested_refs: The Adorno-Marcuse correspondence of 1969, published in New Left Review

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, Hörsaal VI
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by German Wikipedia's article 'Busenattentat': 22 April 1969, Hörsaal VI, three women students, rose and tulip petals, Adorno leaving with his briefcase raised, and his last public appearance. The lecture title is corrected from the research pool's 'Einleitung in dialektisches Denken' to 'Einführung in dialektisches Denken'. Coordinates are the Bockenheim campus.
stops.campa: He is lecturing on Einführung in dialektisches Denken in Hörsaal VI when three women students come up to the lectern, bare their breasts, and scatter rose and tulip petals over him. He takes up his briefcase, holds it in front of his face, and walks out of the hall. Photographs travel round the world within days, and the story hardens into a legend that this killed him four months later, which no medical record supports. He cancels the course and turns to finishing Aesthetic Theory. He never lectures in public again.
suggested_refs: Hito Steyerl, 'Adorno's Grey' (2012), a filmic installation staged around this lecture hall and the legend of its grey paint; Steyerl's own visit and investigation belong to Steyerl, and are cited here only as later engagement with the room

stops.name: Zermatt, the climb to the Gandegghütte
stops.date_confidence: attested by German Wikipedia, which describes the travel to Zermatt, the ascent toward the Gandegghütte at nearly 3,000 m, and preceding heart trouble with medical advice against exertion. Day unknown and defaulted to 01. Coordinates are the Nominatim geocode of the hut, correcting a research-pool figure roughly 750 m off.
stops.campa: On holiday in the Valais he goes up toward the Gandegghütte above Zermatt, climbing to nearly three thousand metres. He has been having heart trouble and has been told not to exert himself. He goes anyway. What the record holds is the altitude, the hut, and the advice disregarded. What it does not hold is anything he said about the mountain, or whether the climb was defiance, or absent-mindedness, or a man of sixty-five wanting to see the glacier once more.

stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by both German and English Wikipedia, which name Visp, the Visper Krankenhaus St. Maria, and the cardiac cause. stops.campa: He is admitted to the St Maria hospital at Visp, in the canton of Valais, and dies there of a heart attack on the sixth of August, five weeks short of his sixty-sixth birthday. Aesthetic Theory is unfinished on his desk in Frankfurt. Gretel will outlive him by twenty-four years. One reference work consulted here gives Frankfurt am Main as his place of death, against the German and English records that give Visp, and the discrepancy is left standing.

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, Ästhetische Theorie
stops.date_confidence: year attested by SEP and English Wikipedia, with Gretel Adorno and Rolf Tiedemann named as editors; month and day defaulted. The Hullot-Kentor translation is dated 1997 by the pool with the note that SEP does not pin the year further. The Nachgelassene Schriften series is attested by SEP as beginning in 1993.
stops.campa: Gretel Adorno and Rolf Tiedemann assemble Ästhetische Theorie out of the typescripts he left, and it is published in 1970. Its subject is how a work of art can be autonomous and a social fact at once, answerable to nothing but its own form and made entirely out of the world's material. Robert Hullot-Kentor's English version calls it a second magnum opus. The Nachgelassene Schriften, the lecture courses and notebooks and correspondence he never sent to a printer, begin appearing in 1993.

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, the glass cube on the Campus Westend
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by German Wikipedia's article 'Adorno-Denkmal': inaugurated 10 October 2003 for the centenary, at what was then Theodor-W.-Adorno-Platz on the Bockenheim campus, and relocated to the Westend campus in April 2016. The coordinates given here are the present Westend location; the monument was not standing there in 2003. This is a posthumous-reception stop, dated by the object rather than by the traveler, on the pattern already used in the Max Horkheimer file's closing segment.
stops.campa: For the centenary the city commissions the artist Vadim Zakharov, and what goes up is a glass cube two and a half metres high, five panels of safety glass at three hundred and fifty kilos each, enclosing a reconstruction of the writing desk, the chair, and the parquet floor. On the desk lie a metronome set diagonally across a book, a first edition of Negative Dialektik, a manuscript, and a musical score. The lamp switches itself on at dusk. Sentences from Minima Moralia and Aesthetic Theory are set into the pavement around it as a labyrinth.
suggested_refs: The Adorno-Denkmal, Goethe-Universität Campus Westend, moved there in April 2016 from Tilly-Edinger-Platz (formerly Theodor-W.-Adorno-Platz), Bockenheim
